coordinate-level starting points for future work, per that document's
finding that no barrier geometry (straight line, stepped polyline, or
general polygon) achieves full HV/SELV pad-center separation on the

confirmed topologically separable (see the analysis doc Sec 6).

single_line_candidate._note: The one documented candidate that predates this analysis (origin/safety/mains-selv-isolation-barrier, commit 645154b7): vertical line at the HV/SELV pad-centroid midpoint. Measured this session at 41.0% pad misclassification (133/324) -- WORSE than the exhaustive axis-aligned best-fit (32.7%, x=21.245 or y=21.223, both degenerate near-edge splits with no real discriminative power). Kept here only as the prior art baseline, not a recommendation.

stepped_polyline_candidate_16band._note: Best 16-band piecewise-vertical split found by this analysis (per-band exhaustive x search). Expressed as 16 IsolationBarrier entries, one per 14.625mm-tall y-band, each independently supported by today's schema (a Vec<IsolationBarrier>, evaluated independently per zone/trace -- see isolation_barrier.rs). Still misclassifies 73/324 pads (22.5%) -- an improvement over the single line's 32.7-41.0%, but far from compliant, and this is the BEST a vertical-segments-only polyline can do: the topological obstruction (Sec 5 of the analysis doc) is not a curve-complexity problem, it recurs within single y-bands as little as ~3mm tall (R27.2 HV vs U10.2 SELV vs R8.1/R8.2 HV vs K1.A2 SELV, all within y=[220.8, 223.8]), which no function-of-y boundary can resolve.
stepped_polyline_candidate_16band.measured_pad_misclassification: 73/324 (22.5%) -- NOT compliant, provided only to demonstrate the schema's existing multi-barrier capability and its measured ceiling on this placement
